newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Fitzwilton says confident of 1996 outturn.
newsitem.headline: Fitzwilton says confident of 1996 outturn.

text.p: Irish industrial holding group Fitzwilton Plc said on Thursday that progress to date led it to be confident of the outcome for the full year.

"The progress which has been made in the first half of the year at Wellworth's and Waterford Wedgwood has continued since then and gives us confidence for the outcome for the year as a whole," chairman Tony O'Reilly said in a results statement.
Fitzwilton reported a rise of 13 percent in first half pre-tax profit to 5.1 million Irish pounds. The group said total sales in Wellworth grew by 9.7 percent and pre-tax profit rose by 10 percent.
O'Reilly said the improvement in earnings from continuing operations reflected both continued growth at Wellworths, a Northern Ireland leading food retailer, and increased profits at
Fitzwilton owns a 12.9 percent stake in crystal and china group Waterford Wedgwood, a company Heinz chief Tony O'Reilly is also chairman of.

The group said margins were satisfactory but trading at Rennicks was slow in the first half of 1996 with profits below expectations. "However this is expected to pick up in the second half of the year," Fitzwilton said.
It said Waterford Wedgwood's growing profits trend continued in the first half of 1996 and Fitzwilton's share of these profits was 1.6 million punts.
The market value of Fitzwilton's holding in Waterford Wedgwood is 70 million punts, it said.
